items.title: 8.13 The effect of a change in pressure or volume

source_refs.note: Topic 8.13, printed pages 180-181, with Quick Check 8.6 carried as a table.

blocks.text: A change of volume or pressure has no effect when the system involves no gases, or when the numbers of moles of gaseous reactants and products are equal in a homogeneous gas equilibrium; it can be discussed only when the gaseous moles of reactants and products are unequal. Consider the Haber synthesis, N2(g) + 3H2(g) giving 2NH3(g). Increase in pressure or decrease in volume: the forward reaction reduces the number of moles and hence the volume, so at equilibrium the mixture occupies less volume than at the start, and raising the pressure produces more ammonia, a shift in the forward direction. Decrease in pressure or increase in volume: the reaction moves to the side that occupies the greater volume, and ammonia synthesis shifts in the reverse direction.

blocks.prompt: In which gaseous equilibrium does pressure have no effect on the position: 2NO2 giving N2O4; PCl5 giving PCl3 + Cl2; CO + H2O giving CO2 + H2; 2SO2 + O2 giving 2SO3?
blocks.explanation: CO + H2O giving CO2 + H2, because it has two moles of gas on each side; a change of pressure or volume affects both sides equally. The other three change the number of gas moles and so shift with pressure.

items: Pressure or volume matters only when gas moles differ: higher pressure (smaller volume) favours the side with fewer gas moles (ammonia synthesis forward); lower pressure the side with more; the position moves, Kc does not.
